anomalies.observed: The anodes of D6, D20, and D22 are all connected to net /NET0066, which has no connection to any power rail. D5, a similar LED, has its anode on +3V3.
anomalies.expected: The common anode net /NET0066 should be connected to a positive supply rail (e.g., +3V3) so the LEDs can be driven by their open-drain cathode signals.
anomalies.impact: D6, D20, and D22 will not illuminate because their anodes are floating and no current path exists from a supply through the LEDs to the open-drain drivers.

anomalies.observed: U12 pin 14 (SDA/VSS) and U21 pin 14 (SDA/VSS) are both tied to the GND net. Their pin 9 (I2C/~SPI) is also tied to GND, selecting I2C mode. The I2C SDA bus net NET0088 contains other I2C devices but not U12 or U21.
anomalies.expected: In I2C mode (pin 9 low), pin 14 is the SDA data line and should be connected to the I2C SDA bus (NET0088), not to GND.
anomalies.impact: The SC16IS752 UARTs U12 and U21 cannot communicate over I2C because their SDA pins are grounded instead of connected to the bus.

anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U2 and U29 have both their primary-side ground (GND1) and secondary-side ground (GND2) connected to the same GND net.
anomalies.expected: For an isolated CAN transceiver, GND1 and GND2 must be separate isolated grounds to maintain galvanic isolation between the logic side and the CAN bus side.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation of both CAN interfaces is defeated, creating a common ground between the CM4 logic side and the CAN bus side, which can cause ground loops, noise, and potential damage.

These deviations would prevent the affected LEDs and UARTs from working and defeat the intended CAN isolation.
